name: plan
description: Create a step-by-step plan for complex tasks. Use this BEFORE executing tools when a task has multiple steps, involves unfamiliar code, or requires coordination across files/systems. Each step should specify what to do, why, and which tool to use. Delegate every substantive step to a subagent - serial or parallel - so each step runs with a clean, focused context and you review the results; keep in the parent only trivial single-tool steps, tightly coupled overlapping edits, and final review/synthesis. Simple tasks (read one file, answer a question, run one command) do NOT need a plan - just act directly.

action.description: What to do in this step (e.g., 'read src/main.rs', 'run cargo build', 'apply patch to fix X').

reason.description: Why this step is needed and what we expect to learn or achieve.

tool.description: Primary tool for this step (e.g. 'read_file', 'execute_command', 'apply_patch', 'knowledge_search'). Use 'none' if no tool is needed.

parallelizable.description: Whether this step can run in parallel with the previous step (no data dependency on earlier steps). Default: false. Only meaningful when set explicitly - it no longer follows from `delegate`; a delegated step is serial unless you set this to true.

delegate.description: Whether this step should be delegated to a subagent. Delegate every substantive step, serial or parallel: the subagent runs with a clean, focused context and you review its result. Serial delegated steps run one at a time via the synchronous `task` (hand the needed context from prior results in the prompt); steps with `parallelizable: true` run concurrently via task_spawn. Keep in the parent only trivial single-tool steps, tightly coupled overlapping edits, and final review/synthesis.

steps.description: Ordered list of steps to accomplish the task.

summary.description: Brief one-line summary of the overall plan.
